Zaccharie Risacher is bringing a different kind of chaos to the Mavericks

Zacch is all over the court, all the time.
ByNoah Weber|Nov 25, 2026, 4:10 PM EST
Add us as a preferred source
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:25
Instaread

The start of Zaccharie Risacher's first season with the Dallas Mavericks has been chaotic, but not in the way you expect.

Most of the time, chaos from a player or a team involves something bad that can destroy a season. Just look at what's going on in Pittsburgh with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

But in Risacher's case, he's not destroying the Mavericks' season. He's destroying other teams' offensive possessions with his defensive intensity and motor.

Zaccharie Risacher is becoming a key defensive weapon in Dallas

He's bringing the good kind of chaos, and it's led to him receiving a significant role in Dusty May's rotation. Zacch is averaging 9.1 points, along with career highs in rebounds (5.1), steals (1.1), and blocks (0.9) per game. A new role with the Mavs has worked wonders for him after a rough ending to his time with the Atlanta Hawks, and May has found the right way to utilize him rather than forcing him into a bigger role than he is comfortable with.

Risacher is one of Dallas' best perimeter defenders, as he brings great effort, moves his feet well, and uses his length to his advantage. His defense on star players has been impressive thus far, and wreaking havoc on that end has become his calling card.

While Risacher's steals and blocks per game are promising, his impact on the defensive end goes beyond the box score. He's averaging 2.9 deflections per game, which rank second on the Mavericks behind only Cooper Flagg.

Risacher is turning defensive chaos into Mavericks offense

Risacher is always getting his hands on the ball in passing lanes, which often leads to steals and points in transition on the other end.

The Mavericks have become pretty dependent on their transition offense due to their struggles in the half-court, and Zacch has played a big role in their success on fast breaks. He has thrown down 19 dunks through 18 games, which averages out to a career-high 1.06 dunks per game. Many of these dunks are coming in transition, as the 6-foot-8 wing uses his speed to run past recovering defenders and get to the basket.

These types of chaos-filled sequences that are filled with deflections, blocks, steals, dunks, and hustle are what have made Risacher special in Dallas, and they have needed this spark. He has stepped up as a starter over the last three games, averaging 12.7 points and 7.0 rebounds per game while shooting 53.3 percent from the field.

Risacher is making an impact despite his shooting struggles

His 3-point shooting is still lagging behind the rest of his game and has unfortunately been the bad kind of chaos. He's shooting 28.6 percent from three, and his release and load-up sometimes vary as he gets set up to let it fly. Risacher has shown some encouraging signs that he can still be a good shooter, making multiple 3-pointers in three games this season, but he needs to become more efficient to become a threat from beyond the arc.

Zacch's energy and effort have become staples of his game as a Maverick, and he's like a bull in a china shop when he's on the court. His high motor helps lead to excellent defense and good transition play, and his performance in these areas has helped him become a key piece in Dallas in his first season with the team.
